title: Studio dates in New York and sitting out the road; Hot Lips Page and Rushing at the Savoy
summary: Tate prefers New York recording work and staying home, and plays with Hot Lips Page and Jimmy Rushing.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I was getting like two, three record dates a day, three and four record dates, man, because during this time, there were a lot of big bands, you know, like integrated bands, cats was calling me when they knew I was out -- you know, like out in Romeo and those cats in Hymie Schertzef and all them cats, they were giving me rings and all that kind of stuff. So we were doing a lot of things for singers. They still had a lot of singers in those days, big bands and things.

And man, I didn't know. I said, "Man, I didn't know it was like this and I don't have to go out of town?" So when they asked me to go -- they asked me to come back to the band. I says, "Uh-uh." Because I had found what I really wanted to -- I could play much more, you know what I mean? And I was meeting cats and I was staying at home with my family. So that's why I didn't go out. So then I worked with Lips, Hot Lips, for a while. He had some theater dates and things and I did some things with him and then who else? Was it Rush? Rush got a band. So I says, "Look --" He was the house band like for Savoy. So Rush said, "Come on, man, join the band. I got all the cats." He had Buck, Emmett, Dickie, Walter Page, had Walter Johnson on drums, another tenor player, who died very young, a hell of a tenor player, Harry Johnson, and himself and a boy named Danny -- I can't think of his name -- Danny. And Jimmy Mundy was writing the arrangements. So I says, "Yeah, I'll go on up here," and I went on up there and went to work with Rush in the Savoy. And let's see, what did I do for him for Savoy? Oh, yeah, Lucille Dixon had a band down in Savannah Club, they had a show down, there, you know. The Savannah Club down on Fourth Street?
